key_insight: The paper shows that quantum circuit expressibility is only meaningful when it is supported by enough data, with learnable circuit complexity scaling like sample size times error squared.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML system design, it provides a principled way to choose ansatz depth from available measurements instead of overbuilding circuits that the data cannot justify.
method: Derive an Occam-style learning bound for n-qubit states preparable with at most G two-qubit gates.
Define best G-gate approximation error d_G(ρ̂) and approximate circuit complexity C_η(ρ̂) for arbitrary quantum sources.
Prove an adaptive model-selection theorem with an oracle inequality that picks circuit complexity from data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical metric-entropy analysis, agnostic learning bounds, and matching lower bounds showing supported gates scale as G_supported ≃ Mε^2 up to logarithmic factors.
watch_item: The result is asymptotic and information-theoretic, so practical performance will still depend on noise, optimization, and whether tomography saturation at 2^n is relevant for the target system.
paper_title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning
